title: Lognormal Stock Price Distributions, Return Compounding, Volatility Estimation, and Black-Scholes Foundations
prerequisites: Basic understanding of continuous compounding and natural logarithms
Standard deviation and variance of statistical samples
European option payoffs and premium structures
learningOutcomes: Explain why stock prices follow a lognormal distribution and how Ito's lemma convexity drag adjusts log return drift ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Differentiate arithmetic average returns from true geometric compounding and calculate mutual fund return distortions ([fact-04], [fact-05]).
Estimate annualized volatility sigma from sample standard deviation s using the 252 trading day convention ([fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
Distinguish terminal gross payoff from net trading profit and understand the core market assumptions of the Black-Scholes-Merton model ([fact-09], [fact-10], [fact-11]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Arithmetic averages severely distort true wealth compounding because volatility creates a drag; a sequence of gains and losses can yield a positive arithmetic average while resulting in zero net geometric return ([fact-04], [fact-05]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Kenneth French's 1980 study proved that weekend variance is only slightly higher than weekday variance, demonstrating that active trading activity itself—not the passage of calendar time—drives volatility ([fact-08]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Gross payoff ignores the initial premium paid to acquire the option; net trading profit is strictly defined as Terminal Gross Payoff minus Premium paid ([fact-09]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: An investor's portfolio starts at $100.00, gains 100% in year 1 to $200.00, and loses 50% in year 2 back to $100.00. Separately, daily stock prices produce a sample standard deviation of daily log returns s = 0.0132 (1.32%).
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What is the arithmetic mean return versus the true geometric compound return? 2) What is the annualized volatility sigma assuming 252 trading days?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Detailed pedagogical explanation grounded in source principles.

coreTakeaways: Continuously compounded stock returns are normally distributed, making stock prices lognormally distributed and ensuring equity values never drop below zero ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Arithmetic return averages upwardly bias performance by sigma^2 / 2, requiring geometric compounding for accurate wealth evaluation ([fact-04], [fact-05]).
Annualized volatility estimated over 252 trading days and rigorous BSM market assumptions form the bedrock of continuous-time option pricing ([fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08], [fact-10], [fact-11]).
